Each cell is joined to the other cells in its row, its column, and its box, seven in all, so a valid Sudoku solution is a proper four-coloring of the graph. Edges along a row or column bow around the cells in between." width="100%"} Creates one node per cell of an `n^2 x n^2` grid (81 cells for the usual `n = 3`), row by row, and joins two cells when they share a row, a column or an `n x n` box. Solving a Sudoku puzzle is exactly finding a proper coloring of this graph with `n^2` colors (the digits) that extends the given clues, so the graph turns puzzles into graph coloring problems. Every cell has `3 n^2 - 2 n - 1` neighbors (20 for `n = 3`), giving `n^4 (3 n^2 - 2 n - 1) / 2` edges (810 for `n = 3`). Orders `0` and `1` have no edges. It is NetworkX's `sudoku_graph()`. With `label=True` each cell is labelled `"(row,col)"`, counting from zero. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier cell (in row-by-row order) to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Sudoku graphs are useful for: - solving and analyzing Sudoku and Latin-square puzzles with coloring algorithms - test graphs with known chromatic number (`n^2`) and many large cliques - teaching graph coloring with a familiar example ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Order of the puzzle: the boxes are `n x n` and the grid `n^2 x n^2`. Default is `3` (the standard 9 x 9 Sudoku). Must be non-negative. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each cell is labelled with its zero-based position as `"(row,col)"`. Because these labels don't depend on the existing nodes, adding a second labelled grid raises `ValueError`; pass `label=False` for it. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The standard Sudoku graph has 81 cells, each with 20 neighbors: ::: {#53bea223 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_sudoku_graph() graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), set(graph.degrees(return_dict=True).values()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (81, 810, {20}) ``` ::: ::: Each row, column and box is a clique of nine cells, so at least nine digits are needed, and a completed Sudoku shows nine are enough: ::: {#bcdcee46 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 9 ``` ::: ::: The 4 x 4 puzzle (`n=2`) is small enough to see a cell's neighbors: its row, its column and the rest of its box: ::: {#65af065c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} small = ec.Graph().add_sudoku_graph(n=2) sorted(small.get_label_from_id(v) for v in small.get_neighbors("(0,0)")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['(0,1)', '(0,2)', '(0,3)', '(1,0)', '(1,1)', '(2,0)', '(3,0)'] ``` ::: :::
